++diff --git a/tests/checkers/test_source_stream.py b/tests/checkers/test_source_stream.py
++new file mode 100644
++index 0000000..0a64fdf
++--- /dev/null
+++++ b/tests/checkers/test_source_stream.py
++@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+++"""Unit tests for python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream.
+++
+++Pins the shared stream read/decode contract (bytes decoded as UTF-8, str passed
+++through) plus source-root containment and trailing-comment splitting.
+++"""
+++
+++from __future__ import annotations
+++
+++import io
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++import astroid
+++import pytest
+++
+++from python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream import (
+++    is_under_source_root,
+++    read_module_source,
+++    split_trailing_comment,
+++)
+++
+++pytestmark = pytest.mark.no_external_api
+++
+++
+++class TestReadModuleSource:
+++    """``read_module_source`` decodes bytes and leaves str untouched."""
+++
+++    def test_binary_stream_decoded_as_utf8(self) -> None:
+++        source = '"""Módulo."""\n\nVALUE = "café"\n'
+++        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++
+++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
+++
+++    def test_text_stream_returned_unchanged(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+++        source = "VALUE = 'café'\n"
+++        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "stream", lambda: io.StringIO(source))
+++
+++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
+++
+++    def test_descendant_node_reads_owning_module(self) -> None:
+++        source = "def factory() -> int:\n    return 1\n"
+++        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++        function = module.body[0]
+++
+++        assert read_module_source(function) == source
+++
+++
+++@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+++    ("path", "roots", "expected"),
+++    [
+++        pytest.param("src/pkg/mod.py", ["src"], True, id="nested-under-root"),
+++        pytest.param("src", ["src"], True, id="root-itself"),
+++        pytest.param("tests/test_mod.py", ["src"], False, id="outside-root"),
+++        pytest.param("lib/mod.py", ["src", "lib"], True, id="second-root"),
+++    ],
+++)
+++def test_is_under_source_root_given_relative_paths_then_expected_bool(
+++    tmp_path: Path,
+++    path: str,
+++    roots: list[str],
+++    expected: bool,
+++) -> None:
+++    (tmp_path / "src").mkdir()
+++    (tmp_path / "lib").mkdir()
+++
+++    assert is_under_source_root(tmp_path / path, [tmp_path / root for root in roots]) is expected
+++
+++
+++@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+++    ("line", "expected"),
+++    [
+++        pytest.param("value = 1  # technical reason", ("value = 1  ", "technical reason"), id="trailing"),
+++        pytest.param("value = 1", ("value = 1", None), id="no-comment"),
+++        pytest.param("# standalone reason", ("", "standalone reason"), id="comment-only"),
+++        pytest.param(
+++            "value = '#not-a-comment'  # real reason", ("value = '#not-a-comment'  ", "real reason"), id="hash-in-string"
+++        ),
+++        pytest.param("value = 1  #no-space", ("value = 1  #no-space", None), id="marker-needs-whitespace"),
+++        pytest.param("value = 1  #  spaced", ("value = 1  ", "spaced"), id="extra-whitespace"),
+++    ],
+++)
+++def test_split_trailing_comment_given_line_then_code_and_comment(
+++    line: str,
+++    expected: tuple[str, str | None],
+++) -> None:
+++    assert split_trailing_comment(line) == expected

++ 
++ Fixture-row data lives in ``tests/checkers/_factories.py`` (free LOC).
++ """

++     emit_coverage_violations,
++@@ -115,7 +116,7 @@ def test_has_main_block_given_code_then_expected_bool(code: str, expected: bool)
++     assert _has_main_block(_parse(code)) is expected
++ 
++ 
++-# ── _is_under_source_root ──────────────────────────────────────────
+++# ── is_under_source_root (shared) ──────────────────────────────────
++ 
++ 
++ @pytest.mark.parametrize(("path", "source_roots", "expected"), _IS_UNDER_SOURCE_ROOT_CASES)
++@@ -125,7 +126,7 @@ def test_is_under_source_root_given_path_and_roots_then_expected_bool(
++     expected: bool,
++ ) -> None:
++     checker, _tc = make_coverage_checker(source_roots=source_roots)

+++    assert is_under_source_root(Path(path), checker._coverage.patterns.source_roots) is expected

+++# Step: QA
+++
+++## Goal
+++Perform independent quality assurance on the item's implementation and test suite. Guard against test weakening, false passes, and unverified claims.
+++
+++## Rules
+++- SKEPTICAL VERIFICATION: do NOT trust developer summaries. Scrutinize engine check results (`red-test`, `test-diff`), actual diffs, and tool outputs.
+++- Test weakening defense: scrutinize `testDiff`. Reject any test change that deletes assertions, relaxes matchers, replaces concrete checks with tautologies, or reduces test coverage.
+++- Story kind validation:
+++  - `dev` stories: verify `red-test` proved tests failed on baseline code and pass after implementation.
+++  - `no-behavior` stories: confirm tests remain materially identical. Functional behavior must not change.
+++- Reviewer boundary: reviewers critique; reviewers NEVER write code fixes. Yield structured output matching `review.schema.json`, using only dispositions allowed by the section below.
+++
+++## Dispositions Criteria
+++Allowed dispositions for this review: fix, optional, architect, human-awareness, human-async.
+++Use ONLY these dispositions; any other disposition value fails validation.
+++# Review Suggestion Dispositions
+++
+++Criteria for assigning disposition to review findings:
+++
+++| Disposition | When to Assign | Engine Action |
+++|---|---|---|
+++| `fix` | Concrete defect, failing gate, broken contract, missing test, or deviation from assignment. | Returns item to `fixLoopTo` step (bounded by `maxFixRounds`); developer must address. Non-item: triggers consult. |
+++| `optional` | Non-blocking polish, code style improvement, minor refactor opportunity, or deferred debt. | Passed to developer if another fix round occurs; otherwise recorded as tech debt for future iterations. |
+++| `architect` | Architectural contradiction, interface redesign, boundary breach, or uncertainty exceeding item scope. | Triggers immediate architect consult; architect's decision is binding and final. |
+++| `human-awareness` | High-impact technical tradeoff or notable choice operator should be aware of, but architect can decide now. | Architect decides immediately; creates informational record in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`. |
+++| `human-async` | Missing business requirement, external credential needed, conflicting user intent requiring operator decision. | Creates blocking entry in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`; item and dependents pause; unrelated items proceed. |
+++
+++## Rules
+++- Defect requiring code change MUST be `fix`.
+++- Do NOT use `architect` for routine bugs; reserve for structural/design conflicts.
+++- Do NOT use `human-async` when repo context or architecture docs provide the answer.
+++

++++## Rules
++++- Target green: every test selector and case identified in `target` MUST pass cleanly.
++++- Quality gates: run project gates via `bash`; all gates MUST succeed with exit code 0.
++++- Sizing budget: keep changes minimal and within the engine-enforced prod-line budget (see agent philosophy). The engine rejects oversized diffs mechanically.
++++- Tool-call budget: aim to finish within ~60 tool calls. Batch reads, prefer `grep`/`ast_grep` over re-reading files, and stop exploring once you can implement — the engine journals a warning above the threshold.
++++- Evidence mandatory: yield `status: ok` with non-empty `evidence` (array of strings detailing personal verification) matching `developer-output.schema.json`.

++++# Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
++++#
++++# Single source of truth for reading astroid module streams (decode-if-bytes
++++# UTF-8) and for interpreting trailing ``# <comment>`` markers. Usage
++++# docstrings live in ``_source_stream.pyi``.
++++
++++from __future__ import annotations
++++
++++import re
++++from pathlib import Path
++++
++++from astroid import nodes
++++from beartype import beartype
++++
++++_TRAILING_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s+(.+)")
++++
++++
++++@beartype
++++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
++++    raw = node.root().stream().read()  # type: ignore[union-attr]  # root() of a parsed node is Module; Module.stream exists
++++    return raw.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw
++++
++++
++++@beartype
++++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
++++    resolved = path.resolve()
++++    for root in source_roots:
++++        try:
++++            resolved.relative_to(root)
++++        except ValueError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort path containment: a non-match is the expected negative result, not an error
++++            continue
++++        return True
++++    return False
++++
++++
++++@beartype
++++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
++++    match = _TRAILING_COMMENT.search(line)
++++    if match is None:
++++        return line, None
++++    return line[: match.start()], match.group(1)

++++"""Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
++++
++++- ``read_module_source`` reads a node's module stream, decoding bytes as UTF-8.
++++- ``is_under_source_root`` checks path containment against source roots.
++++- ``split_trailing_comment`` separates code from a trailing ``# comment``.
++++
++++``_base._is_under_source_root`` remains in place for ``SourceRootMixin``; it is
++++intentionally untouched here and is a future backend-consolidation follow-up.
++++"""
++++
++++from pathlib import Path
++++
++++from astroid import nodes
++++
++++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
++++    """Read the source text backing *node*'s module.
++++
++++    ``astroid`` module streams normally yield ``bytes``; those are decoded as
++++    UTF-8. A text stream is returned unchanged.
++++
++++    Args:
++++        node: Any AST node belonging to the module to read.
++++
++++    Returns:
++++        The module source text as ``str``.
++++
++++    Raises:
++++        AttributeError: If the module has no backing stream.
++++        OSError: If reading the stream fails.
++++    """
++++
++++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
++++    """Check whether *path* resolves inside any of *source_roots*.
++++
++++    Args:
++++        path: Candidate filesystem path.
++++        source_roots: Resolved source-root directories.
++++
++++    Returns:
++++        True if *path* is contained by a source root, False otherwise.
++++    """
++++
++++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
++++    """Split a trailing ``# <comment>`` marker from *line*.
++++
++++    A trailing comment is a ``#`` followed by whitespace and at least one
++++    character (the historical ``#\\s+(.+)`` checker pattern). The returned
++++    comment is the raw text after the whitespace — not stripped — so callers
++++    keep their existing whitespace handling.
++++
++++    Args:
++++        line: One source line, optionally carrying a trailing comment.
++++
++++    Returns:
++++        ``(code, comment)`` where *code* is the text before the comment marker
++++        and *comment* is ``None`` when no trailing comment exists.
++++    """

++++"""Unit tests for python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream.
++++
++++Pins the shared stream read/decode contract (bytes decoded as UTF-8, str passed
++++through) plus source-root containment and trailing-comment splitting.
++++"""
++++
++++from __future__ import annotations
++++
++++import io
++++from pathlib import Path
++++
++++import astroid
++++import pytest
++++
++++from python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream import (
++++    is_under_source_root,
++++    read_module_source,
++++    split_trailing_comment,
++++)
++++
++++pytestmark = pytest.mark.no_external_api
++++
++++
++++class TestReadModuleSource:
++++    """``read_module_source`` decodes bytes and leaves str untouched."""
++++
++++    def test_binary_stream_decoded_as_utf8(self) -> None:
++++        source = '"""Módulo."""\n\nVALUE = "café"\n'
++++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++++
++++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++++
++++    def test_text_stream_returned_unchanged(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
++++        source = "VALUE = 'café'\n"
++++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++++        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "stream", lambda: io.StringIO(source))
++++
++++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++++
++++    def test_descendant_node_reads_owning_module(self) -> None:
++++        source = "def factory() -> int:\n    return 1\n"
++++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++++        function = module.body[0]
++++
++++        assert read_module_source(function) == source
++++
++++
++++@pytest.mark.parametrize(
++++    ("path", "roots", "expected"),
++++    [
++++        pytest.param("src/pkg/mod.py", ["src"], True, id="nested-under-root"),
++++        pytest.param("src", ["src"], True, id="root-itself"),
++++        pytest.param("tests/test_mod.py", ["src"], False, id="outside-root"),
++++        pytest.param("lib/mod.py", ["src", "lib"], True, id="second-root"),
++++    ],
++++)
++++def test_is_under_source_root_given_relative_paths_then_expected_bool(
++++    tmp_path: Path,
++++    path: str,
++++    roots: list[str],
++++    expected: bool,
++++) -> None:
++++    (tmp_path / "src").mkdir()
++++    (tmp_path / "lib").mkdir()
++++
++++    assert is_under_source_root(tmp_path / path, [tmp_path / root for root in roots]) is expected
++++
++++
++++@pytest.mark.parametrize(

++++        pytest.param("# standalone reason", ("", "standalone reason"), id="comment-only"),
++++        pytest.param(
++++            "value = '#not-a-comment'  # real reason", ("value = '#not-a-comment'  ", "real reason"), id="hash-in-string"
++++        ),
++++        pytest.param("value = 1  #no-space", ("value = 1  #no-space", None), id="marker-needs-whitespace"),
++++        pytest.param("value = 1  #  spaced", ("value = 1  ", "spaced"), id="extra-whitespace"),
++++    ],
++++)

+++# Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
+++#
+++# Single source of truth for reading astroid module streams (decode-if-bytes
+++# UTF-8) and for interpreting trailing ``# <comment>`` markers. Usage
+++# docstrings live in ``_source_stream.pyi``.
+++
+++from __future__ import annotations
+++
+++import re
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++from astroid import nodes
+++from beartype import beartype
+++
+++_TRAILING_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s+(.+)")
+++
+++
+++@beartype
+++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
+++    raw = node.root().stream().read()  # type: ignore[union-attr]  # root() of a parsed node is Module; Module.stream exists
+++    return raw.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw
+++
+++
+++@beartype
+++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
+++    resolved = path.resolve()
+++    for root in source_roots:
+++        try:
+++            resolved.relative_to(root)
+++        except ValueError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort path containment: a non-match is the expected negative result, not an error
+++            continue
+++        return True
+++    return False
+++
+++
+++@beartype
+++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+++    match = _TRAILING_COMMENT.search(line)
+++    if match is None:
+++        return line, None
+++    return line[: match.start()], match.group(1)

+++++ b/src/python_setup_lint/checkers/_source_stream.pyi
++@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+++"""Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
+++
+++- ``read_module_source`` reads a node's module stream, decoding bytes as UTF-8.
+++- ``is_under_source_root`` checks path containment against source roots.
+++- ``split_trailing_comment`` separates code from a trailing ``# comment``.
+++
+++``_base._is_under_source_root`` remains in place for ``SourceRootMixin``; it is
+++intentionally untouched here and is a future backend-consolidation follow-up.
+++"""
+++
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++from astroid import nodes
+++
+++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
+++    """Read the source text backing *node*'s module.
+++
+++    ``astroid`` module streams normally yield ``bytes``; those are decoded as
+++    UTF-8. A text stream is returned unchanged.
+++
+++    Args:
+++        node: Any AST node belonging to the module to read.
+++
+++    Returns:
+++        The module source text as ``str``.
+++
+++    Raises:
+++        AttributeError: If the module has no backing stream.
+++        OSError: If reading the stream fails.
+++    """
+++
+++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
+++    """Check whether *path* resolves inside any of *source_roots*.
+++
+++    Args:
+++        path: Candidate filesystem path.
+++        source_roots: Resolved source-root directories.
+++
+++    Returns:
+++        True if *path* is contained by a source root, False otherwise.
+++    """
+++
+++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+++    """Split a trailing ``# <comment>`` marker from *line*.
+++
+++    A trailing comment is a ``#`` followed by whitespace and at least one
+++    character (the historical ``#\\s+(.+)`` checker pattern). The returned
+++    comment is the raw text after the whitespace — not stripped — so callers
+++    keep their existing whitespace handling.
+++
+++    Args:
+++        line: One source line, optionally carrying a trailing comment.
+++
+++    Returns:
+++        ``(code, comment)`` where *code* is the text before the comment marker
+++        and *comment* is ``None`` when no trailing comment exists.
+++    """

++# Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
++#
++# Single source of truth for reading astroid module streams (decode-if-bytes
++# UTF-8) and for interpreting trailing ``# <comment>`` markers. Usage
++# docstrings live in ``_source_stream.pyi``.
++
++from __future__ import annotations
++
++import re
++from pathlib import Path
++
++from astroid import nodes
++from beartype import beartype
++
++_TRAILING_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s+(.+)")
++
++
++@beartype
++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
++    raw = node.root().stream().read()  # type: ignore[union-attr]  # root() of a parsed node is Module; Module.stream exists
++    return raw.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw
++
++
++@beartype
++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
++    resolved = path.resolve()
++    for root in source_roots:
++        try:
++            resolved.relative_to(root)
++        except ValueError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort path containment: a non-match is the expected negative result, not an error
++            continue
++        return True
++    return False
++
++
++@beartype
++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
++    match = _TRAILING_COMMENT.search(line)
++    if match is None:
++        return line, None
++    return line[: match.start()], match.group(1)

++"""Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
++
++- ``read_module_source`` reads a node's module stream, decoding bytes as UTF-8.
++- ``is_under_source_root`` checks path containment against source roots.
++- ``split_trailing_comment`` separates code from a trailing ``# comment``.
++
++``_base._is_under_source_root`` remains in place for ``SourceRootMixin``; it is
++intentionally untouched here and is a future backend-consolidation follow-up.
++"""
++
++from pathlib import Path
++
++from astroid import nodes
++
++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
++    """Read the source text backing *node*'s module.
++
++    ``astroid`` module streams normally yield ``bytes``; those are decoded as
++    UTF-8. A text stream is returned unchanged.
++
++    Args:
++        node: Any AST node belonging to the module to read.
++
++    Returns:
++        The module source text as ``str``.
++
++    Raises:
++        AttributeError: If the module has no backing stream.
++        OSError: If reading the stream fails.
++    """
++
++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
++    """Check whether *path* resolves inside any of *source_roots*.
++
++    Args:
++        path: Candidate filesystem path.
++        source_roots: Resolved source-root directories.
++
++    Returns:
++        True if *path* is contained by a source root, False otherwise.
++    """
++
++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
++    """Split a trailing ``# <comment>`` marker from *line*.
++
++    A trailing comment is a ``#`` followed by whitespace and at least one
++    character (the historical ``#\\s+(.+)`` checker pattern). The returned
++    comment is the raw text after the whitespace — not stripped — so callers
++    keep their existing whitespace handling.
++
++    Args:
++        line: One source line, optionally carrying a trailing comment.
++
++    Returns:
++        ``(code, comment)`` where *code* is the text before the comment marker
++        and *comment* is ``None`` when no trailing comment exists.
++    """

++
++Pins the shared stream read/decode contract (bytes decoded as UTF-8, str passed
++through) plus source-root containment and trailing-comment splitting.
++"""
++
++from __future__ import annotations
++
++import io

++

++class TestReadModuleSource:
++    """``read_module_source`` decodes bytes and leaves str untouched."""
++
++    def test_binary_stream_decoded_as_utf8(self) -> None:
++        source = '"""Módulo."""\n\nVALUE = "café"\n'
++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++
++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++
++    def test_text_stream_returned_unchanged(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
++        source = "VALUE = 'café'\n"
++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "stream", lambda: io.StringIO(source))
++
++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++
++    def test_descendant_node_reads_owning_module(self) -> None:
++        source = "def factory() -> int:\n    return 1\n"
++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++        function = module.body[0]
++
++        assert read_module_source(function) == source
++

+# Step: Review
+
+## Goal
+Conduct adversarial peer code review on completed changes, evaluating implementation quality against requested focus criteria.
+
+## Rules
+- SKEPTICAL SCRUTINY: base findings on actual git diff and codebase state, never developer summaries.
+- Focus dimensions (see agent definition for the full philosophy and dispositions guide):
+  - `code`: validate clarity, wrapper discipline, complexity limits, boundary validation, and error typing.
+  - `security`: audit input sanitization, injection vectors, command execution boundaries, and secret exposure risks.
+  - `consistency`: ensure conformance with established repository naming idioms, directory layouts, and design patterns.
+  - `result`: for spikes (`fact-finder`, `poc`, `test-assumptions`), confirm findings answer the core uncertainty and code is properly isolated.
+- Reviewer boundary: reviewers critique; reviewers NEVER write fixes. Yield structured output matching `review.schema.json`, using only dispositions allowed by the section below.
+
+## Dispositions Criteria
+Allowed dispositions for this review: fix, optional, architect, human-awareness, human-async.
+Use ONLY these dispositions; any other disposition value fails validation.
+# Review Suggestion Dispositions
+
+Criteria for assigning disposition to review findings:
+
+| Disposition | When to Assign | Engine Action |
+|---|---|---|
+| `fix` | Concrete defect, failing gate, broken contract, missing test, or deviation from assignment. | Returns item to `fixLoopTo` step (bounded by `maxFixRounds`); developer must address. Non-item: triggers consult. |
+| `optional` | Non-blocking polish, code style improvement, minor refactor opportunity, or deferred debt. | Passed to developer if another fix round occurs; otherwise recorded as tech debt for future iterations. |
+| `architect` | Architectural contradiction, interface redesign, boundary breach, or uncertainty exceeding item scope. | Triggers immediate architect consult; architect's decision is binding and final. |
+| `human-awareness` | High-impact technical tradeoff or notable choice operator should be aware of, but architect can decide now. | Architect decides immediately; creates informational record in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`. |
+| `human-async` | Missing business requirement, external credential needed, conflicting user intent requiring operator decision. | Creates blocking entry in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`; item and dependents pause; unrelated items proceed. |
+
+## Rules
+- Defect requiring code change MUST be `fix`.
+- Do NOT use `architect` for routine bugs; reserve for structural/design conflicts.
+- Do NOT use `human-async` when repo context or architecture docs provide the answer.
+
+## Assignment

API (all in _source_stream, @beartype, decode-if-bytes UTF-8 preserving current semantics — item reports exact bytes/str handling verified by tests; tach-clean; <=500 + .pyi): read_module_source(node)->str; is_under_source_root(path, source_roots)->bool (pure; coverage.py migrates its local checker-bound helper to this, passing checker._coverage.patterns.source_roots; _base keeps its existing helper untouched — coexistence documented, future consolidation is backend follow-up); split_trailing_comment(line)->tuple[code, comment|None] adopted by suppression/bare-except trailing paths where mechanical (preceding-comment paths keep local logic unless identical — item reports which). Enumerate sites via grep \\.stream\\(\\) at HEAD (report full list; expect suppression/bare-except/stub families, verify) and replace all (grep zero copies outside helper). Verify: grep zero local copies; git diff -- _base.py _base.pyi empty; no new failures vs M1 table; golden hash-equal or shift-reported.",

++
++        +"""Unit tests for python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream.
++
++        +
++
++        +Pins the shared stream read/decode contract (bytes decoded as UTF-8,
++        str passed
++
++        +through) plus source-root containment and trailing-comment splitting.
++
++        +"""
++
++        +
++
++        +from __future__ import annotations
++
++        +
++
++        +import io
++
++        +from pathlib import Path
++
++        +
++
++        +import astroid
++
++        +import pytest
++
++        +
++
++        +from python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream import (
++
++        +    is_under_source_root,
++
++        +    read_module_source,
++
++        +    split_trailing_comment,
++
++        +)
++
++        +
++
++        +pytestmark = pytest.mark.no_external_api
++
++        +
++
++        +
++
++        +class TestReadModuleSource:
++
++        +    """``read_module_source`` decodes bytes and leaves str
++        untouched."""
++
++        +
++
++        +    def test_binary_stream_decoded_as_utf8(self) -> None:
++
++        +        source = '"""Módulo."""\n\nVALUE = "café"\n'
++
++        +        module = astroid.parse(source)
++
++        +
++
++        +        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++
++        +
++
++        +    def test_text_stream_returned_unchanged(self, monkeypatch:
++        pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
++
++        +        source = "VALUE = 'café'\n"
++
++        +        module = astroid.parse(source)
++
++        +        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "stream", lambda:
++        io.StringIO(source))
++
++        +
++
++        +        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++
++        +
++
++        +    def test_descendant_node_reads_owning_module(self) -> None:
++
++        +        source = "def factory() -> int:\n    return 1\n"
++
++        +        module = astroid.parse(source)
++
++        +        function = module.body[0]
++
++        +
++
++        +        assert read_module_source(function) == source
++
++        +
++
++        +
++
++        +@pytest.mark.parametrize(
++
++        +    ("path", "roots", "expected"),
++
++        +    [
++
++        +        pytest.param("src/pkg/mod.py", ["src"], True,
++        id="nested-under-root"),
++
++        +        pytest.param("src", ["src"], True, id="root-itself"),
++
++        +        pytest.param("tests/test_mod.py", ["src"], False,
++        id="outside-root"),
++
++        +        pytest.param("lib/mod.py", ["src", "lib"], True,
++        id="second-root"),
++
++        +    ],
++
++        +)
++
++        +def test_is_under_source_root_given_relative_paths_then_expected_bool(
++
++        +    tmp_path: Path,
++
++        +    path: str,
++
++        +    roots: list[str],
++
++        +    expected: bool,
++
++        +) -> None:
++
++        +    (tmp_path / "src").mkdir()
++
++        +    (tmp_path / "lib").mkdir()
++
++        +
++
++        +    assert is_under_source_root(tmp_path / path, [tmp_path / root for
++        root in roots]) is expected
++
++        +
++
++        +
++
++        +@pytest.mark.parametrize(
++
++        +    ("line", "expected"),
++
++        +    [
++
++        +        pytest.param("value = 1  # technical reason", ("value = 1  ",
++        "technical reason"), id="trailing"),
++
++        +        pytest.param("value = 1", ("value = 1", None),
++        id="no-comment"),
++
++        +        pytest.param("# standalone reason", ("", "standalone reason"),
++        id="comment-only"),
++
++        +        pytest.param(
++
++        +            "value = '#not-a-comment'  # real reason", ("value =
++        '#not-a-comment'  ", "real reason"), id="hash-in-string"
++
++        +        ),
++
++        +        pytest.param("value = 1  #no-space", ("value = 1  #no-space",
++        None), id="marker-needs-whitespace"),
++
++        +        pytest.param("value = 1  #  spaced", ("value = 1  ", "spaced"),
++        id="extra-whitespace"),
++
++        +    ],
++
++        +)
++
++        +def test_split_trailing_comment_given_line_then_code_and_comment(
++
++        +    line: str,
++
++        +    expected: tuple[str, str | None],
++

++# Step: QA
++
++## Goal
++Perform independent quality assurance on the item's implementation and test suite. Guard against test weakening, false passes, and unverified claims.
++
++## Rules
++- SKEPTICAL VERIFICATION: do NOT trust developer summaries. Scrutinize engine check results (`red-test`, `test-diff`), actual diffs, and tool outputs.
++- Test weakening defense: scrutinize `testDiff`. Reject any test change that deletes assertions, relaxes matchers, replaces concrete checks with tautologies, or reduces test coverage.
++- Story kind validation:
++  - `dev` stories: verify `red-test` proved tests failed on baseline code and pass after implementation.
++  - `no-behavior` stories: confirm tests remain materially identical. Functional behavior must not change.
++- Reviewer boundary: reviewers critique; reviewers NEVER write code fixes. Yield structured output matching `review.schema.json`, using only dispositions allowed by the section below.
++
++## Dispositions Criteria
++Allowed dispositions for this review: fix, optional, architect, human-awareness, human-async.
++Use ONLY these dispositions; any other disposition value fails validation.
++# Review Suggestion Dispositions
++
++Criteria for assigning disposition to review findings:
++
++| Disposition | When to Assign | Engine Action |
++|---|---|---|
++| `fix` | Concrete defect, failing gate, broken contract, missing test, or deviation from assignment. | Returns item to `fixLoopTo` step (bounded by `maxFixRounds`); developer must address. Non-item: triggers consult. |
++| `optional` | Non-blocking polish, code style improvement, minor refactor opportunity, or deferred debt. | Passed to developer if another fix round occurs; otherwise recorded as tech debt for future iterations. |
++| `architect` | Architectural contradiction, interface redesign, boundary breach, or uncertainty exceeding item scope. | Triggers immediate architect consult; architect's decision is binding and final. |
++| `human-awareness` | High-impact technical tradeoff or notable choice operator should be aware of, but architect can decide now. | Architect decides immediately; creates informational record in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`. |
++| `human-async` | Missing business requirement, external credential needed, conflicting user intent requiring operator decision. | Creates blocking entry in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`; item and dependents pause; unrelated items proceed. |
++
++## Rules
++- Defect requiring code change MUST be `fix`.
++- Do NOT use `architect` for routine bugs; reserve for structural/design conflicts.
++- Do NOT use `human-async` when repo context or architecture docs provide the answer.
++
++## Assignment

API (all in _source_stream, @beartype, decode-if-bytes UTF-8 preserving current semantics — item reports exact bytes/str handling verified by tests; tach-clean; <=500 + .pyi): read_module_source(node)->str; is_under_source_root(path, source_roots)->bool (pure; coverage.py migrates its local checker-bound helper to this, passing checker._coverage.patterns.source_roots; _base keeps its existing helper untouched — coexistence documented, future consolidation is backend follow-up); split_trailing_comment(line)->tuple[code, comment|None] adopted by suppression/bare-except trailing paths where mechanical (preceding-comment paths keep local logic unless identical — item reports which). Enumerate sites via grep \\.stream\\(\\) at HEAD (report full list; expect suppression/bare-except/stub families, verify) and replace all (grep zero copies outside helper). +++## Goal
+++Implement production code changes and supporting tests to satisfy the assignment, make declared targets pass green, and pass all project gates.
+++
+++## Rules
+++- Target green: every test selector and case identified in `target` MUST pass cleanly.
+++- Quality gates: run project gates via `bash`; all gates MUST succeed with exit code 0.
+++- Sizing budget: keep changes minimal and within the engine-enforced prod-line budget (see agent philosophy). The engine rejects oversized diffs mechanically.
+++- Tool-call budget: aim to finish within ~60 tool calls. Batch reads, prefer `grep`/`ast_grep` over re-reading files, and stop exploring once you can implement — the engine journals a warning above the threshold.
+++- Evidence mandatory: yield `status: ok` with non-empty `evidence` (array of strings detailing personal verification) matching `developer-output.schema.json`.

+++# Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
+++#
+++# Single source of truth for reading astroid module streams (decode-if-bytes
+++# UTF-8) and for interpreting trailing ``# <comment>`` markers. Usage
+++# docstrings live in ``_source_stream.pyi``.
+++
+++from __future__ import annotations
+++
+++import re
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++from astroid import nodes
+++from beartype import beartype
+++
+++_TRAILING_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s+(.+)")
+++
+++
+++@beartype
+++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
+++    raw = node.root().stream().read()  # type: ignore[union-attr]  # root() of a parsed node is Module; Module.stream exists
+++    return raw.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw
+++
+++
+++@beartype
+++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
+++    resolved = path.resolve()
+++    for root in source_roots:
+++        try:
+++            resolved.relative_to(root)
+++        except ValueError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort path containment: a non-match is the expected negative result, not an error
+++            continue
+++        return True
+++    return False
+++
+++
+++@beartype
+++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+++    match = _TRAILING_COMMENT.search(line)
+++    if match is None:
+++        return line, None
+++    return line[: match.start()], match.group(1)

+++"""Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
+++
+++- ``read_module_source`` reads a node's module stream, decoding bytes as UTF-8.
+++- ``is_under_source_root`` checks path containment against source roots.
+++- ``split_trailing_comment`` separates code from a trailing ``# comment``.
+++
+++``_base._is_under_source_root`` remains in place for ``SourceRootMixin``; it is
+++intentionally untouched here and is a future backend-consolidation follow-up.
+++"""
+++
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++from astroid import nodes
+++
+++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
+++    """Read the source text backing *node*'s module.
+++
+++    ``astroid`` module streams normally yield ``bytes``; those are decoded as
+++    UTF-8. A text stream is returned unchanged.
+++
+++    Args:
+++        node: Any AST node belonging to the module to read.
+++
+++    Returns:
+++        The module source text as ``str``.
+++
+++    Raises:
+++        AttributeError: If the module has no backing stream.
+++        OSError: If reading the stream fails.
+++    """
+++
+++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
+++    """Check whether *path* resolves inside any of *source_roots*.
+++
+++    Args:
+++        path: Candidate filesystem path.
+++        source_roots: Resolved source-root directories.
+++
+++    Returns:
+++        True if *path* is contained by a source root, False otherwise.
+++    """
+++
+++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+++    """Split a trailing ``# <comment>`` marker from *line*.
+++
+++    A trailing comment is a ``#`` followed by whitespace and at least one
+++    character (the historical ``#\\s+(.+)`` checker pattern). The returned
+++    comment is the raw text after the whitespace — not stripped — so callers
+++    keep their existing whitespace handling.
+++
+++    Args:
+++        line: One source line, optionally carrying a trailing comment.
+++
+++    Returns:
+++        ``(code, comment)`` where *code* is the text before the comment marker
+++        and *comment* is ``None`` when no trailing comment exists.
+++    """

+++"""Unit tests for python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream.
+++
+++Pins the shared stream read/decode contract (bytes decoded as UTF-8, str passed
+++through) plus source-root containment and trailing-comment splitting.
+++"""
+++
+++from __future__ import annotations
+++
+++import io
+++from pathlib import Path
+++

+++
+++class TestReadModuleSource:
+++    """``read_module_source`` decodes bytes and leaves str untouched."""
+++
+++    def test_binary_stream_decoded_as_utf8(self) -> None:
+++        source = '"""Módulo."""\n\nVALUE = "café"\n'
+++        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++
+++        assert read_module_source(module) == source

+++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
+++

+++
+++        assert read_module_source(function) == source

+++
+++        +"""Unit tests for python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream.
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +Pins the shared stream read/decode contract (bytes decoded as UTF-8,
+++        str passed
+++
+++        +through) plus source-root containment and trailing-comment splitting.
+++
+++        +"""
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +from __future__ import annotations
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +import io
+++
+++        +from pathlib import Path
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +import astroid
+++
+++        +import pytest
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +from python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream import (
+++
+++        +    is_under_source_root,
+++
+++        +    read_module_source,
+++
+++        +    split_trailing_comment,
+++
+++        +)
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +pytestmark = pytest.mark.no_external_api
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +class TestReadModuleSource:
+++
+++        +    """``read_module_source`` decodes bytes and leaves str
+++        untouched."""
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +    def test_binary_stream_decoded_as_utf8(self) -> None:
+++
+++        +        source = '"""Módulo."""\n\nVALUE = "café"\n'
+++
+++        +        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +        assert read_module_source(module) == source
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +    def test_text_stream_returned_unchanged(self, monkeypatch:
+++        pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+++
+++        +        source = "VALUE = 'café'\n"
+++
+++        +        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++
+++        +        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "stream", lambda:
+++        io.StringIO(source))
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +        assert read_module_source(module) == source
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +    def test_descendant_node_reads_owning_module(self) -> None:
+++
+++        +        source = "def factory() -> int:\n    return 1\n"
+++
+++        +        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++
+++        +        function = module.body[0]
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +        assert read_module_source(function) == source
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +
+++
+++        +@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+++
+++        +    ("path", "roots", "expected"),
+++
+++        +    [
+++
+++        +        pytest.param("src/pkg/mod.py", ["src"], True,

+++# Step: QA
+++
+++## Goal
+++Perform independent quality assurance on the item's implementation and test suite. Guard against test weakening, false passes, and unverified claims.
+++
+++## Rules
+++- SKEPTICAL VERIFICATION: do NOT trust developer summaries. Scrutinize engine check results (`red-test`, `test-diff`), actual diffs, and tool outputs.
+++- Test weakening defense: scrutinize `testDiff`. Reject any test change that deletes assertions, relaxes matchers, replaces concrete checks with tautologies, or reduces test coverage.
+++- Story kind validation:
+++  - `dev` stories: verify `red-test` proved tests failed on baseline code and pass after implementation.
+++  - `no-behavior` stories: confirm tests remain materially identical. Functional behavior must not change.
+++- Reviewer boundary: reviewers critique; reviewers NEVER write code fixes. Yield structured output matching `review.schema.json`, using only dispositions allowed by the section below.
+++
+++## Dispositions Criteria
+++Allowed dispositions for this review: fix, optional, architect, human-awareness, human-async.
+++Use ONLY these dispositions; any other disposition value fails validation.
+++# Review Suggestion Dispositions
+++
+++Criteria for assigning disposition to review findings:
+++
+++| Disposition | When to Assign | Engine Action |
+++|---|---|---|
+++| `fix` | Concrete defect, failing gate, broken contract, missing test, or deviation from assignment. | Returns item to `fixLoopTo` step (bounded by `maxFixRounds`); developer must address. Non-item: triggers consult. |
+++| `optional` | Non-blocking polish, code style improvement, minor refactor opportunity, or deferred debt. | Passed to developer if another fix round occurs; otherwise recorded as tech debt for future iterations. |
+++| `architect` | Architectural contradiction, interface redesign, boundary breach, or uncertainty exceeding item scope. | Triggers immediate architect consult; architect's decision is binding and final. |
+++| `human-awareness` | High-impact technical tradeoff or notable choice operator should be aware of, but architect can decide now. | Architect decides immediately; creates informational record in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`. |
+++| `human-async` | Missing business requirement, external credential needed, conflicting user intent requiring operator decision. | Creates blocking entry in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`; item and dependents pause; unrelated items proceed. |
+++
+++## Rules
+++- Defect requiring code change MUST be `fix`.
+++- Do NOT use `architect` for routine bugs; reserve for structural/design conflicts.
+++- Do NOT use `human-async` when repo context or architecture docs provide the answer.
+++

++++# Step: Develop
++++
++++## Goal
++++Implement production code changes and supporting tests to satisfy the assignment, make declared targets pass green, and pass all project gates.
++++
++++## Rules
++++- Target green: every test selector and case identified in `target` MUST pass cleanly.
++++- Quality gates: run project gates via `bash`; all gates MUST succeed with exit code 0.
++++- Sizing budget: keep changes minimal and within the engine-enforced prod-line budget (see agent philosophy). The engine rejects oversized diffs mechanically.
++++- Tool-call budget: aim to finish within ~60 tool calls. Batch reads, prefer `grep`/`ast_grep` over re-reading files, and stop exploring once you can implement — the engine journals a warning above the threshold.
++++- Evidence mandatory: yield `status: ok` with non-empty `evidence` (array of strings detailing personal verification) matching `developer-output.schema.json`.
++++

++++# Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
++++#
++++# Single source of truth for reading astroid module streams (decode-if-bytes
++++# UTF-8) and for interpreting trailing ``# <comment>`` markers. Usage
++++# docstrings live in ``_source_stream.pyi``.
++++
++++from __future__ import annotations
++++
++++import re
++++from pathlib import Path
++++
++++from astroid import nodes
++++from beartype import beartype
++++
++++_TRAILING_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s+(.+)")
++++
++++
++++@beartype
++++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
++++    raw = node.root().stream().read()  # type: ignore[union-attr]  # root() of a parsed node is Module; Module.stream exists
++++    return raw.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw
++++
++++
++++@beartype
++++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
++++    resolved = path.resolve()
++++    for root in source_roots:
++++        try:
++++            resolved.relative_to(root)
++++        except ValueError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort path containment: a non-match is the expected negative result, not an error
++++            continue
++++        return True
++++    return False
++++
++++
++++@beartype
++++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
++++    match = _TRAILING_COMMENT.search(line)
++++    if match is None:
++++        return line, None
++++    return line[: match.start()], match.group(1)

++++"""Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
++++
++++- ``read_module_source`` reads a node's module stream, decoding bytes as UTF-8.
++++- ``is_under_source_root`` checks path containment against source roots.
++++- ``split_trailing_comment`` separates code from a trailing ``# comment``.
++++
++++``_base._is_under_source_root`` remains in place for ``SourceRootMixin``; it is
++++intentionally untouched here and is a future backend-consolidation follow-up.
++++"""
++++
++++from pathlib import Path
++++
++++from astroid import nodes
++++
++++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
++++    """Read the source text backing *node*'s module.
++++
++++    ``astroid`` module streams normally yield ``bytes``; those are decoded as
++++    UTF-8. A text stream is returned unchanged.
++++
++++    Args:
++++        node: Any AST node belonging to the module to read.
++++
++++    Returns:
++++        The module source text as ``str``.
++++
++++    Raises:
++++        AttributeError: If the module has no backing stream.
++++        OSError: If reading the stream fails.
++++    """
++++
++++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
++++    """Check whether *path* resolves inside any of *source_roots*.
++++
++++    Args:
++++        path: Candidate filesystem path.
++++        source_roots: Resolved source-root directories.
++++
++++    Returns:
++++        True if *path* is contained by a source root, False otherwise.
++++    """
++++
++++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
++++    """Split a trailing ``# <comment>`` marker from *line*.
++++
++++    A trailing comment is a ``#`` followed by whitespace and at least one
++++    character (the historical ``#\\s+(.+)`` checker pattern). The returned
++++    comment is the raw text after the whitespace — not stripped — so callers
++++    keep their existing whitespace handling.
++++
++++    Args:
++++        line: One source line, optionally carrying a trailing comment.
++++
++++    Returns:
++++        ``(code, comment)`` where *code* is the text before the comment marker
++++        and *comment* is ``None`` when no trailing comment exists.
++++    """

++++"""Unit tests for python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream.
++++
++++Pins the shared stream read/decode contract (bytes decoded as UTF-8, str passed
++++through) plus source-root containment and trailing-comment splitting.
++++"""
++++
++++from __future__ import annotations
++++
++++import io
++++from pathlib import Path
++++
++++import astroid

++++)

++++class TestReadModuleSource:
++++    """``read_module_source`` decodes bytes and leaves str untouched."""
++++
++++    def test_binary_stream_decoded_as_utf8(self) -> None:
++++        source = '"""Módulo."""\n\nVALUE = "café"\n'
++++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++++
++++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++++
++++    def test_text_stream_returned_unchanged(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
++++        source = "VALUE = 'café'\n"
++++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++++        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "stream", lambda: io.StringIO(source))
++++
++++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++++
++++    def test_descendant_node_reads_owning_module(self) -> None:
++++        source = "def factory() -> int:\n    return 1\n"
++++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++++        function = module.body[0]
++++
++++        assert read_module_source(function) == source
++++

+++# Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
+++#
+++# Single source of truth for reading astroid module streams (decode-if-bytes
+++# UTF-8) and for interpreting trailing ``# <comment>`` markers. Usage
+++# docstrings live in ``_source_stream.pyi``.
+++
+++from __future__ import annotations
+++
+++import re
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++from astroid import nodes
+++from beartype import beartype
+++
+++_TRAILING_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s+(.+)")
+++
+++
+++@beartype
+++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
+++    raw = node.root().stream().read()  # type: ignore[union-attr]  # root() of a parsed node is Module; Module.stream exists
+++    return raw.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw
+++
+++
+++@beartype
+++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
+++    resolved = path.resolve()
+++    for root in source_roots:
+++        try:
+++            resolved.relative_to(root)
+++        except ValueError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort path containment: a non-match is the expected negative result, not an error
+++            continue
+++        return True
+++    return False
+++
+++
+++@beartype
+++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+++    match = _TRAILING_COMMENT.search(line)
+++    if match is None:
+++        return line, None
+++    return line[: match.start()], match.group(1)

++@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+++"""Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
+++
+++- ``read_module_source`` reads a node's module stream, decoding bytes as UTF-8.
+++- ``is_under_source_root`` checks path containment against source roots.
+++- ``split_trailing_comment`` separates code from a trailing ``# comment``.
+++
+++``_base._is_under_source_root`` remains in place for ``SourceRootMixin``; it is
+++intentionally untouched here and is a future backend-consolidation follow-up.
+++"""
+++
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++from astroid import nodes
+++
+++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
+++    """Read the source text backing *node*'s module.
+++
+++    ``astroid`` module streams normally yield ``bytes``; those are decoded as
+++    UTF-8. A text stream is returned unchanged.
+++
+++    Args:
+++        node: Any AST node belonging to the module to read.
+++
+++    Returns:
+++        The module source text as ``str``.
+++
+++    Raises:
+++        AttributeError: If the module has no backing stream.
+++        OSError: If reading the stream fails.
+++    """
+++
+++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
+++    """Check whether *path* resolves inside any of *source_roots*.
+++
+++    Args:
+++        path: Candidate filesystem path.
+++        source_roots: Resolved source-root directories.
+++
+++    Returns:
+++        True if *path* is contained by a source root, False otherwise.
+++    """
+++
+++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+++    """Split a trailing ``# <comment>`` marker from *line*.
+++
+++    A trailing comment is a ``#`` followed by whitespace and at least one
+++    character (the historical ``#\\s+(.+)`` checker pattern). The returned
+++    comment is the raw text after the whitespace — not stripped — so callers
+++    keep their existing whitespace handling.
+++
+++    Args:
+++        line: One source line, optionally carrying a trailing comment.
+++
+++    Returns:
+++        ``(code, comment)`` where *code* is the text before the comment marker
+++        and *comment* is ``None`` when no trailing comment exists.
+++    """

++new file mode 100644
++index 0000000..0a64fdf
++--- /dev/null
+++++ b/tests/checkers/test_source_stream.py
++@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+++"""Unit tests for python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream.
+++
+++Pins the shared stream read/decode contract (bytes decoded as UTF-8, str passed
+++through) plus source-root containment and trailing-comment splitting.
+++"""
+++
+++from __future__ import annotations
+++
+++import io
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++import astroid
+++import pytest
+++
+++from python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream import (
+++    is_under_source_root,
+++    read_module_source,
+++    split_trailing_comment,
+++)
+++
+++pytestmark = pytest.mark.no_external_api
+++
+++
+++class TestReadModuleSource:
+++    """``read_module_source`` decodes bytes and leaves str untouched."""
+++
+++    def test_binary_stream_decoded_as_utf8(self) -> None:
+++        source = '"""Módulo."""\n\nVALUE = "café"\n'
+++        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++
+++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
+++
+++    def test_text_stream_returned_unchanged(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+++        source = "VALUE = 'café'\n"
+++        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "stream", lambda: io.StringIO(source))
+++
+++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
+++
+++    def test_descendant_node_reads_owning_module(self) -> None:
+++        source = "def factory() -> int:\n    return 1\n"
+++        module = astroid.parse(source)
+++        function = module.body[0]
+++
+++        assert read_module_source(function) == source
+++
+++
+++@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+++    ("path", "roots", "expected"),
+++    [
+++        pytest.param("src/pkg/mod.py", ["src"], True, id="nested-under-root"),
+++        pytest.param("src", ["src"], True, id="root-itself"),
+++        pytest.param("tests/test_mod.py", ["src"], False, id="outside-root"),
+++        pytest.param("lib/mod.py", ["src", "lib"], True, id="second-root"),
+++    ],
+++)
+++def test_is_under_source_root_given_relative_paths_then_expected_bool(
+++    tmp_path: Path,
+++    path: str,
+++    roots: list[str],
+++    expected: bool,
+++) -> None:
+++    (tmp_path / "src").mkdir()
+++    (tmp_path / "lib").mkdir()
+++
+++    assert is_under_source_root(tmp_path / path, [tmp_path / root for root in roots]) is expected
+++
+++
+++@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+++    ("line", "expected"),
+++    [
+++        pytest.param("value = 1  # technical reason", ("value = 1  ", "technical reason"), id="trailing"),
+++        pytest.param("value = 1", ("value = 1", None), id="no-comment"),
+++        pytest.param("# standalone reason", ("", "standalone reason"), id="comment-only"),
+++        pytest.param(
+++            "value = '#not-a-comment'  # real reason", ("value = '#not-a-comment'  ", "real reason"), id="hash-in-string"
+++        ),
+++        pytest.param("value = 1  #no-space", ("value = 1  #no-space", None), id="marker-needs-whitespace"),
+++        pytest.param("value = 1  #  spaced", ("value = 1  ", "spaced"), id="extra-whitespace"),
+++    ],
+++)
+++def test_split_trailing_comment_given_line_then_code_and_comment(
+++    line: str,
+++    expected: tuple[str, str | None],
+++) -> None:
+++    assert split_trailing_comment(line) == expected

++-``_resolve_stub``, ``_index_stub_declarations``, ``emit_coverage_violations``.
+++``_is_trivial_test_data``, ``_has_main_block``, ``_resolve_stub``,
+++``_index_stub_declarations``, ``emit_coverage_violations``; plus the shared
+++``_source_stream.is_under_source_root`` wired to the configured source roots.
++ 
++ Fixture-row data lives in ``tests/checkers/_factories.py`` (free LOC).
++ """

++     _resolve_stub,
++     emit_coverage_violations,
++@@ -115,7 +116,7 @@ def test_has_main_block_given_code_then_expected_bool(code: str, expected: bool)

+++# ── is_under_source_root (shared) ──────────────────────────────────
++ 
++ 
++ @pytest.mark.parametrize(("path", "source_roots", "expected"), _IS_UNDER_SOURCE_ROOT_CASES)
++@@ -125,7 +126,7 @@ def test_is_under_source_root_given_path_and_roots_then_expected_bool(
++     expected: bool,
++ ) -> None:
++     checker, _tc = make_coverage_checker(source_roots=source_roots)
++-    assert _is_under_source_root(checker, Path(path)) is expected
+++    assert is_under_source_root(Path(path), checker._coverage.patterns.source_roots) is expected

++# Step: QA
++
++## Goal
++Perform independent quality assurance on the item's implementation and test suite. Guard against test weakening, false passes, and unverified claims.
++
++## Rules
++- SKEPTICAL VERIFICATION: do NOT trust developer summaries. Scrutinize engine check results (`red-test`, `test-diff`), actual diffs, and tool outputs.
++- Test weakening defense: scrutinize `testDiff`. Reject any test change that deletes assertions, relaxes matchers, replaces concrete checks with tautologies, or reduces test coverage.
++- Story kind validation:
++  - `dev` stories: verify `red-test` proved tests failed on baseline code and pass after implementation.
++  - `no-behavior` stories: confirm tests remain materially identical. Functional behavior must not change.
++- Reviewer boundary: reviewers critique; reviewers NEVER write code fixes. Yield structured output matching `review.schema.json`, using only dispositions allowed by the section below.
++
++## Dispositions Criteria
++Allowed dispositions for this review: fix, optional, architect, human-awareness, human-async.
++Use ONLY these dispositions; any other disposition value fails validation.
++# Review Suggestion Dispositions
++
++Criteria for assigning disposition to review findings:
++
++| Disposition | When to Assign | Engine Action |
++|---|---|---|
++| `fix` | Concrete defect, failing gate, broken contract, missing test, or deviation from assignment. | Returns item to `fixLoopTo` step (bounded by `maxFixRounds`); developer must address. Non-item: triggers consult. |
++| `optional` | Non-blocking polish, code style improvement, minor refactor opportunity, or deferred debt. | Passed to developer if another fix round occurs; otherwise recorded as tech debt for future iterations. |
++| `architect` | Architectural contradiction, interface redesign, boundary breach, or uncertainty exceeding item scope. | Triggers immediate architect consult; architect's decision is binding and final. |
++| `human-awareness` | High-impact technical tradeoff or notable choice operator should be aware of, but architect can decide now. | Architect decides immediately; creates informational record in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`. |
++| `human-async` | Missing business requirement, external credential needed, conflicting user intent requiring operator decision. | Creates blocking entry in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`; item and dependents pause; unrelated items proceed. |
++
++## Rules
++- Defect requiring code change MUST be `fix`.
++- Do NOT use `architect` for routine bugs; reserve for structural/design conflicts.
++- Do NOT use `human-async` when repo context or architecture docs provide the answer.
++

+++## Goal
+++Implement production code changes and supporting tests to satisfy the assignment, make declared targets pass green, and pass all project gates.
+++
+++## Rules
+++- Target green: every test selector and case identified in `target` MUST pass cleanly.
+++- Quality gates: run project gates via `bash`; all gates MUST succeed with exit code 0.
+++- Sizing budget: keep changes minimal and within the engine-enforced prod-line budget (see agent philosophy). The engine rejects oversized diffs mechanically.
+++- Tool-call budget: aim to finish within ~60 tool calls. Batch reads, prefer `grep`/`ast_grep` over re-reading files, and stop exploring once you can implement — the engine journals a warning above the threshold.
+++- Evidence mandatory: yield `status: ok` with non-empty `evidence` (array of strings detailing personal verification) matching `developer-output.schema.json`.

+++# Step: QA
+++
+++## Goal
+++Perform independent quality assurance on the item's implementation and test suite. Guard against test weakening, false passes, and unverified claims.
+++
+++## Rules
+++- SKEPTICAL VERIFICATION: do NOT trust developer summaries. Scrutinize engine check results (`red-test`, `test-diff`), actual diffs, and tool outputs.
+++- Test weakening defense: scrutinize `testDiff`. Reject any test change that deletes assertions, relaxes matchers, replaces concrete checks with tautologies, or reduces test coverage.
+++- Story kind validation:
+++  - `dev` stories: verify `red-test` proved tests failed on baseline code and pass after implementation.
+++  - `no-behavior` stories: confirm tests remain materially identical. Functional behavior must not change.
+++- Reviewer boundary: reviewers critique; reviewers NEVER write code fixes. Yield structured output matching `review.schema.json`, using only dispositions allowed by the section below.
+++
+++## Dispositions Criteria
+++Allowed dispositions for this review: fix, optional, architect, human-awareness, human-async.
+++Use ONLY these dispositions; any other disposition value fails validation.
+++# Review Suggestion Dispositions
+++
+++Criteria for assigning disposition to review findings:
+++
+++| Disposition | When to Assign | Engine Action |
+++|---|---|---|
+++| `fix` | Concrete defect, failing gate, broken contract, missing test, or deviation from assignment. | Returns item to `fixLoopTo` step (bounded by `maxFixRounds`); developer must address. Non-item: triggers consult. |
+++| `optional` | Non-blocking polish, code style improvement, minor refactor opportunity, or deferred debt. | Passed to developer if another fix round occurs; otherwise recorded as tech debt for future iterations. |
+++| `architect` | Architectural contradiction, interface redesign, boundary breach, or uncertainty exceeding item scope. | Triggers immediate architect consult; architect's decision is binding and final. |
+++| `human-awareness` | High-impact technical tradeoff or notable choice operator should be aware of, but architect can decide now. | Architect decides immediately; creates informational record in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`. |
+++| `human-async` | Missing business requirement, external credential needed, conflicting user intent requiring operator decision. | Creates blocking entry in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`; item and dependents pause; unrelated items proceed. |
+++
+++## Rules
+++- Defect requiring code change MUST be `fix`.
+++- Do NOT use `architect` for routine bugs; reserve for structural/design conflicts.
+++- Do NOT use `human-async` when repo context or architecture docs provide the answer.
+++
+++## Assignment

API (all in _source_stream, @beartype, decode-if-bytes UTF-8 preserving current semantics — item reports exact bytes/str handling verified by tests; tach-clean; <=500 + .pyi): read_module_source(node)->str; is_under_source_root(path, source_roots)->bool (pure; coverage.py migrates its local checker-bound helper to this, passing checker._coverage.patterns.source_roots; _base keeps its existing helper untouched — coexistence documented, future consolidation is backend follow-up); split_trailing_comment(line)->tuple[code, comment|None] adopted by suppression/bare-except trailing paths where mechanical (preceding-comment paths keep local logic unless identical — item reports which). Enumerate sites via grep \\.stream\\(\\) at HEAD (report full list; expect suppression/bare-except/stub families, verify) and replace all (grep zero copies outside helper). Verify: grep zero local copies; git diff -- _base.py _base.pyi empty; no new failures vs M1 table; golden hash-equal or shift-reported.",

++++# Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
++++#
++++# Single source of truth for reading astroid module streams (decode-if-bytes
++++# UTF-8) and for interpreting trailing ``# <comment>`` markers. Usage
++++# docstrings live in ``_source_stream.pyi``.
++++
++++from __future__ import annotations
++++
++++import re
++++from pathlib import Path
++++
++++from astroid import nodes
++++from beartype import beartype
++++
++++_TRAILING_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s+(.+)")
++++
++++
++++@beartype
++++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
++++    raw = node.root().stream().read()  # type: ignore[union-attr]  # root() of a parsed node is Module; Module.stream exists
++++    return raw.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw
++++
++++
++++@beartype
++++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
++++    resolved = path.resolve()
++++    for root in source_roots:
++++        try:
++++            resolved.relative_to(root)
++++        except ValueError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort path containment: a non-match is the expected negative result, not an error
++++            continue
++++        return True
++++    return False
++++
++++
++++@beartype
++++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
++++    match = _TRAILING_COMMENT.search(line)
++++    if match is None:
++++        return line, None
++++    return line[: match.start()], match.group(1)

++++"""Shared source-stream helpers for conformance and stub checkers.
++++
++++- ``read_module_source`` reads a node's module stream, decoding bytes as UTF-8.
++++- ``is_under_source_root`` checks path containment against source roots.
++++- ``split_trailing_comment`` separates code from a trailing ``# comment``.
++++
++++``_base._is_under_source_root`` remains in place for ``SourceRootMixin``; it is
++++intentionally untouched here and is a future backend-consolidation follow-up.
++++"""
++++
++++from pathlib import Path
++++
++++from astroid import nodes
++++
++++def read_module_source(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> str:
++++    """Read the source text backing *node*'s module.
++++
++++    ``astroid`` module streams normally yield ``bytes``; those are decoded as
++++    UTF-8. A text stream is returned unchanged.
++++
++++    Args:
++++        node: Any AST node belonging to the module to read.
++++
++++    Returns:
++++        The module source text as ``str``.
++++
++++    Raises:
++++        AttributeError: If the module has no backing stream.
++++        OSError: If reading the stream fails.
++++    """
++++
++++def is_under_source_root(path: Path, source_roots: list[Path]) -> bool:
++++    """Check whether *path* resolves inside any of *source_roots*.
++++
++++    Args:
++++        path: Candidate filesystem path.
++++        source_roots: Resolved source-root directories.
++++
++++    Returns:
++++        True if *path* is contained by a source root, False otherwise.
++++    """
++++
++++def split_trailing_comment(line: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
++++    """Split a trailing ``# <comment>`` marker from *line*.
++++
++++    A trailing comment is a ``#`` followed by whitespace and at least one
++++    character (the historical ``#\\s+(.+)`` checker pattern). The returned
++++    comment is the raw text after the whitespace — not stripped — so callers
++++    keep their existing whitespace handling.
++++
++++    Args:
++++        line: One source line, optionally carrying a trailing comment.
++++
++++    Returns:
++++        ``(code, comment)`` where *code* is the text before the comment marker
++++        and *comment* is ``None`` when no trailing comment exists.
++++    """

+++index 97af366..8ea9f57 100644
+++--- a/src/python_setup_lint/checkers/conformance/bare_except_comment_checker.py
++++++ b/src/python_setup_lint/checkers/conformance/bare_except_comment_checker.py
+++@@ -1,6 +1,5 @@
+++ from __future__ import annotations
+++ 
+++-import re
+++ from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+++ 
+++ from astroid import nodes
+++@@ -13,6 +12,7 @@ from python_setup_lint.checkers._base import (
+++     _msgs,
+++     check_if_meaningful,
+++ )
++++from python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream import read_module_source, split_trailing_comment
+++ 
+++ if TYPE_CHECKING:
+++     from pylint.lint import PyLinter
+++@@ -77,18 +77,10 @@ class BareExceptCommentChecker(BaseChecker):
+++             True if a justifying comment is found in the source.
+++         """
+++         try:
+++-            stream = node.root().stream()  # type: ignore[union-attr]  # ModuleNode has stream() at runtime
+++-        except AttributeError, OSError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort stream access fallback; logging would noise unavoidable attribute/IO degrade
++++            source = read_module_source(node)
++++        except AttributeError, OSError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort source read fallback; logging would noise unavoidable attribute/IO degrade
+++             return False
+++ 
+++-        if stream is None:
+++-            return False
+++-        try:
+++-            raw = stream.read()
+++-        except OSError:  # pylint: disable=W9740  # best-effort stream read fallback; logging would noise unavoidable IO degrade
+++-            return False
+++-        source = raw.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw
+++-
+++         lines = source.splitlines(keepends=True)
+++ 
+++         lineno = node.fromlineno
+++@@ -97,9 +89,9 @@ class BareExceptCommentChecker(BaseChecker):
+++

+++         line = lines[lineno - 1] if lineno <= len(lines) else ""
+++-        trailing_match = re.search(r"#\s+(.+)", line)
+++-        if trailing_match:

++++        _, comment = split_trailing_comment(line)
++++        if comment is not None:
++++            comment_text = comment.strip()

+++                 rule="bare-except-comment",

++++"""Unit tests for python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream.
++++
++++Pins the shared stream read/decode contract (bytes decoded as UTF-8, str passed
++++through) plus source-root containment and trailing-comment splitting.
++++"""
++++
++++from __future__ import annotations
++++
++++import io
++++from pathlib import Path
++++
++++import astroid
++++import pytest
++++
++++from python_setup_lint.checkers._source_stream import (
++++    is_under_source_root,
++++    read_module_source,
++++    split_trailing_comment,
++++)
++++
++++pytestmark = pytest.mark.no_external_api
++++
++++
++++class TestReadModuleSource:
++++    """``read_module_source`` decodes bytes and leaves str untouched."""
++++
++++    def test_binary_stream_decoded_as_utf8(self) -> None:
++++        source = '"""Módulo."""\n\nVALUE = "café"\n'
++++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++++
++++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++++
++++    def test_text_stream_returned_unchanged(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
++++        source = "VALUE = 'café'\n"
++++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++++        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "stream", lambda: io.StringIO(source))
++++
++++        assert read_module_source(module) == source
++++
++++    def test_descendant_node_reads_owning_module(self) -> None:
++++        source = "def factory() -> int:\n    return 1\n"
++++        module = astroid.parse(source)
++++        function = module.body[0]
++++
++++        assert read_module_source(function) == source
++++
++++
++++@pytest.mark.parametrize(
++++    ("path", "roots", "expected"),
++++    [
++++        pytest.param("src/pkg/mod.py", ["src"], True, id="nested-under-root"),
++++        pytest.param("src", ["src"], True, id="root-itself"),
++++        pytest.param("tests/test_mod.py", ["src"], False, id="outside-root"),
++++        pytest.param("lib/mod.py", ["src", "lib"], True, id="second-root"),
++++    ],
++++)
++++def test_is_under_source_root_given_relative_paths_then_expected_bool(
++++    tmp_path: Path,
++++    path: str,
++++    roots: list[str],
++++    expected: bool,
++++) -> None:
++++    (tmp_path / "src").mkdir()
++++    (tmp_path / "lib").mkdir()
++++
++++    assert is_under_source_root(tmp_path / path, [tmp_path / root for root in roots]) is expected
++++
++++
++++@pytest.mark.parametrize(
++++    ("line", "expected"),
++++    [
++++        pytest.param("value = 1  # technical reason", ("value = 1  ", "technical reason"), id="trailing"),
++++        pytest.param("value = 1", ("value = 1", None), id="no-comment"),
++++        pytest.param("# standalone reason", ("", "standalone reason"), id="comment-only"),
++++        pytest.param(
++++            "value = '#not-a-comment'  # real reason", ("value = '#not-a-comment'  ", "real reason"), id="hash-in-string"
++++        ),
++++        pytest.param("value = 1  #no-space", ("value = 1  #no-space", None), id="marker-needs-whitespace"),
++++        pytest.param("value = 1  #  spaced", ("value = 1  ", "spaced"), id="extra-whitespace"),
++++    ],
++++)
++++def test_split_trailing_comment_given_line_then_code_and_comment(
++++    line: str,
++++    expected: tuple[str, str | None],
++++) -> None:
++++    assert split_trailing_comment(line) == expected

++++# Step: QA
++++
++++## Goal
++++Perform independent quality assurance on the item's implementation and test suite. Guard against test weakening, false passes, and unverified claims.
++++
++++## Rules
++++- SKEPTICAL VERIFICATION: do NOT trust developer summaries. Scrutinize engine check results (`red-test`, `test-diff`), actual diffs, and tool outputs.
++++- Test weakening defense: scrutinize `testDiff`. Reject any test change that deletes assertions, relaxes matchers, replaces concrete checks with tautologies, or reduces test coverage.
++++- Story kind validation:
++++  - `dev` stories: verify `red-test` proved tests failed on baseline code and pass after implementation.
++++  - `no-behavior` stories: confirm tests remain materially identical. Functional behavior must not change.
++++- Reviewer boundary: reviewers critique; reviewers NEVER write code fixes. Yield structured output matching `review.schema.json`, using only dispositions allowed by the section below.
++++
++++## Dispositions Criteria
++++Allowed dispositions for this review: fix, optional, architect, human-awareness, human-async.
++++Use ONLY these dispositions; any other disposition value fails validation.
++++# Review Suggestion Dispositions
++++
++++Criteria for assigning disposition to review findings:
++++
++++| Disposition | When to Assign | Engine Action |
++++|---|---|---|
++++| `fix` | Concrete defect, failing gate, broken contract, missing test, or deviation from assignment. | Returns item to `fixLoopTo` step (bounded by `maxFixRounds`); developer must address. Non-item: triggers consult. |
++++| `optional` | Non-blocking polish, code style improvement, minor refactor opportunity, or deferred debt. | Passed to developer if another fix round occurs; otherwise recorded as tech debt for future iterations. |
++++| `architect` | Architectural contradiction, interface redesign, boundary breach, or uncertainty exceeding item scope. | Triggers immediate architect consult; architect's decision is binding and final. |
++++| `human-awareness` | High-impact technical tradeoff or notable choice operator should be aware of, but architect can decide now. | Architect decides immediately; creates informational record in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`. |
++++| `human-async` | Missing business requirement, external credential needed, conflicting user intent requiring operator decision. | Creates blocking entry in `steer/tousertoreview/{id}.yaml`; item and dependents pause; unrelated items proceed. |
++++
++++## Rules
++++- Defect requiring code change MUST be `fix`.
++++- Do NOT use `architect` for routine bugs; reserve for structural/design conflicts.
++++- Do NOT use `human-async` when repo context or architecture docs provide the answer.
++++
++++## Assignment
